topics.label: Course Welcome and Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its learning objectives concerning cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional non-targeted cancer therapies, detailing their mechanisms of tissue elimination, systemic toxicities, and cellular resistance pathways.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic approaches designed to target cancer cells through their intrinsic biological vulnerabilities and repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeted Kinase Inhibitors and Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the rational design of small-molecule kinase inhibitors against oncogenic drivers and the diverse molecular pathways through which tumors develop resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the application of engineered antibodies to selectively target surface antigens on cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell Modulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the interaction between tumors and the immune system, focusing on therapeutic strategies that activate and engineer T cells to eliminate cancer.

topics.label: Challenges, Progress, and Future Directions in Cancer Care
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader landscape of cancer treatment, assessing overall therapeutic progress, persistent clinical challenges, and future care paradigms.
